transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I guess I'm here because I've been in a bit of a slump? Well, maybe more than a slump, I don't know if that's the right word. I just... I don't seem to care about anything anymore. I hope it's okay to just come right out and say that. 

But, um, yeah. Things I used to really enjoy, like my art classes or going to board-game nights... I just don't care. Even hiking, or, you know, getting back to my soccer team... I just can't bring myself to do any of it. I mostly just sit in my room now while everything sort of... slips away. I know I should be trying harder, and I feel awful about it, I just... does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you can help people with?
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um, well... I guess it really became a constant thing around the summer? Like, last summer. So, I think it's been about a year and four months now. 

I know I probably should have asked for help way before this, and I feel really bad that I let it go on for so long without doing anything. I just kept hoping I would bounce back and, you know, not have to bother anyone with it. I hope you're not disappointed that I waited so long to come in... is that the kind of timeline you were asking for?
Did something stressful happen around the time this started?

Um, well... I guess, actually, if I really think about it... it might have been a little longer than I just said. I'm sorry, I didn't mean to give you the wrong timeline. It's just... well, my husband and I got divorced. 

And, um, this all really started shortly after that. So, I guess it's actually been about a year and eleven months now? I know I should have been able to handle it better, and I really tried to just push through and be okay, but... yeah. It started right after the divorce. I hope it's alright that I corrected myself, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Before this began after your divorce, had you ever had another period in your life when you felt depressed or lost interest in things for weeks at a time?

Um... no, not that I can remember. I mean, I've had normal days where I felt a little down, like anyone else, I guess? But never anything like this, and definitely not for weeks at a time. Before the divorce, I was always pretty active and involved in things. 

I hope that's a good thing? Like, maybe it means it's just tied to the divorce and it'll be easier to fix? I really want to be a good patient and get back to normal, so whatever you think is best... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the answers you need. Is that helpful?
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

Um... well... I guess I've had some passing thoughts, but nothing I would actually act on, I promise. I don't want to sound dramatic or anything. 

It's just... sometimes things feel so heavy, and I keep having these thoughts that I just don't want to wake up anymore. Just to have a break from it all, you know? And... well, my friend came over recently, and I guess she heard me saying out loud that I couldn't keep living like this. I was so embarrassed that she heard that, and I really don't want you to think I'm giving up. I know I need to be stronger. I'm trying really hard to stay positive. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not worrying you too much.
How much has this been affecting your ability to manage everyday responsibilities?

Um... well, I really want to say I'm keeping up with everything, because I know I should be. But... I guess it's actually been pretty hard lately. I'm sorry, I don't want to sound like I'm just letting everything go. 

But I... I stopped taking on my freelance art-education work. I just couldn't focus on it, and I didn't want to do a bad job for anyone. And I've been missing a lot of community events, and my soccer games... I just haven't had the energy, even though I know I should go. 

And, um... my friend actually has been coming over to check on me a lot. I'm really lucky to have her, but I feel terrible that she has to do it. She just wants to make sure I'm... you know, eating and showering, and just being safe, since I've been struggling with that a bit. I know I need to do better, and I'm really trying to get back on track. I hope you don't think I'm completely falling apart. I just want to be honest so you can tell me what I need to fix. Is that okay?
For at least two weeks at a time, have you felt depressed or unable to enjoy things nearly every day?

Um... yes, I guess so. I really don't want to sound like I'm just complaining, but... yeah, it's been pretty much every day for a while now. 

Most days I wake up with this... this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. It's like... I don't know, like there's no future for me beyond my apartment walls. I'm really trying to shake it off, I promise I am. I know I should be looking on the bright side and finding things to enjoy, but it's just been really hard to feel happy about anything lately. I hope that's the kind of information you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right so you can help me.
Have other people noticed that you’ve been moving or speaking more slowly than usual?

Um... well, my friend has mentioned something about that, actually. I really hope I'm not being too much of a burden on her, but she did say I've been acting a little... different. 

I guess... well, I try to keep it together, I really do. But sometimes, I just can't seem to sit still. I'll just pace back and forth, from the kitchen to the window, over and over until my legs actually start aching. I know it's silly, and I'm trying to stop doing it so much. 

But then other days, it's like the exact opposite. I just feel so... heavy. Like, even just trying to make a cup of coffee feels like I'm trying to lift wet cement. Everything just takes so much effort, and I know I probably look like I'm moving in slow motion. I'm really sorry if that sounds strange... I'm trying my best to push through it and act normal. Is that the kind of thing you meant? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Since the divorce, have there been any stretches of at least 2 months when you felt mostly back to your usual self?

Um... I really wish I could say yes, because I know I should be doing better by now. But... no, I don't think I've had a solid two months where I felt completely like my old self again. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds like I'm just wallowing or not trying hard enough. I really am trying to bounce back, I promise. I try to put on a brave face, and there are definitely okay days here and there where I push through it, but... a whole two months in a row? I just haven't been able to string that together yet. 

I hope it's alright that I'm admitting that... I feel like I should be stronger, but I just want to give you the right answers so I can finally get this fixed. Is that helpful?
Have you had any experiences like hearing voices when no one was there, or strongly believing something that others said wasn’t true?

Um... well... I know this is probably going to sound really strange, and I hope you don't think I'm completely losing my mind or anything. I've been really hesitant to tell anyone this because I don't want to seem... you know, crazy. 

But... yes, sometimes I do hear something. It's... it's a woman's voice. She usually comes from the corner of my bedroom. I know it sounds impossible because I live alone, but she sounds so real. Like, as clear as if you were standing right next to my bed talking to me. 

She... she says some really awful things. She tells me that I ruined everything, and that I need to just stay inside where I belong. I try so hard to ignore her, I really do. I know I shouldn't listen to it, and I'm trying my best to just focus on getting better. I hope telling you this doesn't make you think less of me... I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the pieces so you know how to help. Is it... is it okay that I shared that?
